name: Tomatoes
directSow: Not usually recommended in short seasons
transplant: After nights are reliably warm and soil has warmed
spacing: 18-24 in between plants; 30-36 in between rows
rotationNotes: Avoid following tomatoes, peppers, eggplants, or potatoes when disease pressure has been high.

name: Peppers
directSow: Not recommended in most temperate gardens
transplant: After nights are warm; peppers dislike cold soil
spacing: 18-24 in between plants; 24-36 in between rows
rotationNotes: Rotate with other nightshades in mind; avoid recently diseased tomato or potato beds.

name: Lettuce
directSow: As soon as soil can be worked; repeat in cool weather
spacing: 6-12 in depending on harvest stage
rotationNotes: Useful filler crop; avoid crowding where airflow is poor.

name: Beans
directSow: After soil warms and frost danger has passed
spacing: Bush beans 4-6 in; pole beans 6-8 in with support
rotationNotes: Useful before heavy-feeding crops when residues are returned to the soil.

name: Cucumbers
directSow: After soil is warm
transplant: After frost; protect roots during transplanting
spacing: 12-18 in on trellis; more for sprawling plants
rotationNotes: Rotate away from squash, melons, and cucumbers where wilt or mildew has been severe.

name: Carrots
directSow: Early spring through midsummer depending on climate
spacing: 1-3 in after thinning; 12-18 in between rows
rotationNotes: Follow crops that leave soil loose and relatively weed-free.

name: Potatoes
directSow: Plant seed potatoes in cool spring soil
spacing: 10-12 in between seed pieces; 30-36 in between rows
rotationNotes: Avoid following tomatoes, peppers, eggplants, or potatoes.

name: Peas
directSow: Early spring as soon as soil can be worked
spacing: 2-3 in with support for taller varieties
rotationNotes: Good early crop before fall brassicas or greens.

name: Beets
directSow: Spring and late summer
spacing: 3-4 in between plants; 12-18 in between rows
rotationNotes: Useful in succession plantings; thin for both greens and roots.

name: Onions
directSow: Possible for scallions and some climates
transplant: Early spring for seedlings or sets
spacing: 4-6 in for bulbs; closer for scallions
rotationNotes: Avoid following alliums where onion maggot or disease has been a problem.

name: Kale
directSow: Spring or late summer
spacing: 12-18 in between plants
rotationNotes: Rotate with cabbage-family disease and pest cycles in mind.

name: Radishes
directSow: Spring and fall in short successions
spacing: 1-2 in for small radishes; more for daikon
rotationNotes: Fast crop; avoid planting repeatedly where flea beetles are severe.

name: Bok Choy
directSow: Spring or late summer
spacing: 6-12 in depending on full-size or baby harvest
rotationNotes: Watch brassica pest pressure; fall crops are often easier than spring crops.

name: Mizuna
directSow: Spring and fall
spacing: 4-8 in for cut greens; wider for full plants
rotationNotes: Works well as a shoulder-season green.

name: Swiss Chard
directSow: Spring through midsummer
spacing: 8-12 in between plants
rotationNotes: Often bridges spring, summer, and fall better than spinach.

name: Zucchini
directSow: After soil warms
spacing: 24-36 in between plants
rotationNotes: Avoid following cucurbits where squash bugs, borers, or mildew have built up.

name: Winter Squash
directSow: After soil warms
spacing: 36-72 in depending on vine length
rotationNotes: Give a long rotation where cucurbit disease or insect pressure is high.

name: Corn
directSow: After soil warms; sow in blocks for pollination
spacing: 8-12 in in blocks; 24-36 in between rows
rotationNotes: Heavy feeder; follows legumes well when fertility is managed.

name: Spinach
directSow: Early spring, late summer, or fall depending on climate
spacing: 4-6 in for mature plants; closer for baby leaf
rotationNotes: Use cool windows; heat and long days trigger bolting.

name: Garlic
directSow: Plant cloves in fall before ground freezes
spacing: 4-6 in between cloves; 8-12 in between rows
rotationNotes: Keep alliums out of the same bed for several years where disease pressure exists.

name: Arugula
directSow: Spring and late summer through early fall
transplant: Possible when young but rarely needed
spacing: 2-4 in for baby leaf; 6 in for mature plants
rotationNotes: Treat as a brassica when tracking flea beetles and cabbage-family disease pressure.

name: Turnips
directSow: Spring and late summer for roots or greens
spacing: 2-4 in for small roots; wider for large varieties
rotationNotes: Rotate with other brassicas and watch flea beetle pressure on young leaves.

name: Collards
directSow: Spring or late summer
spacing: 12-18 in for regular harvest; wider for full plants
rotationNotes: Rotate with cabbage-family crops and remove heavily infested residues.
